title: Garlic Bread
subtitle: A simple side loaf with garlic butter and parsley
excerpt: A soft bread dough spread with garlic butter and baked until crisp. This is the side dish that disappears first.
sourceNotes: Garlic bread as a baked side dish became popular in Italian-American cooking in the mid-20th century. The version made from a whole baked loaf split and filled with garlic butter is now ubiquitous in British homes.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the shaped and buttered loaf before baking. Bake from frozen at 200C for 25 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the dough and garlic butter a day ahead. Bring to room temperature before baking.

content.text: You will need 7g fast-action yeast and 1 teaspoon of salt for the dough, plus a pinch of sugar to activate the yeast.
Mix the flour, 7g yeast, 1 teaspoon salt and a pinch of sugar in a large bowl.
Add 250ml of warm water. Mix to a soft dough.
Knead on a floured surface for 8 minutes until smooth.
Put in a lightly oiled bowl. Cover and prove for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Beat the butter with the garlic and parsley. Season with a pinch of salt.
Knock back the dough and shape into a baton. Place on a lined baking tray.
Cut deep slashes across the top every 2cm. Spread the garlic butter generously into each slash and over the top.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until golden and crisp at the edges.
Serve hot straight from the oven.

items.cause: Yeast was dead or water was too hot.
items.fix: Use hand-warm water (not hot) and check yeast is in date.

items.cause: Butter was spread too thinly on exposed areas.
items.fix: Press butter deep into the slashes rather than over the surface.

items.symptom: Bread is doughy in the centre.
items.cause: Loaf was too thick or oven too hot.
items.fix: Flatten slightly before baking to help the centre cook through.
